clue.text: Common habit of man and oaf, stifling tortured genius

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the word for oaf wraps around the other letters

parts.note: an oaf is a lout, a clumsy boor

indicators.note: tortured means twisted out of shape, so the letters of genius are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that ordinary men and louts dress alike, smothering some suffering genius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common habit' suggests a routine, but a habit here is clothing: what an ordinary man wears to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge suit is the ordinary business attire, the everyday outfit worn by a man.

clue.text: Cat making sound of course

indicators.note: making sound of says the word for course is heard, not seen, giving letters that sound alike

parts.note: a links is a golf course by the sea

explanation.surface: A cat that naturally makes some noise.
explanation.walkthrough: A LINKS is a seaside golf course, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild member of the feline family with tufted ears.

clue.text: . Plotting is not over

definitions.meaning: scheming, as in asking what someone is scheming at
no more than, as in a maximum of ten

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both scheming at something and at most a given amount, so it fits both senses.

clue.text: Nab blighter concealing underhand delivery for seasoned traveller

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so one piece sits within the other pair

parts.note: to nab is to get hold of
a lob is a ball bowled or thrown underarm
a blighter is a rotter, a contemptible person

explanation.surface: Catch the scoundrel who is hiding an underarm throw, aimed at a much-travelled person.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket and rounders a lob is a ball delivered underarm, which is why 'underhand delivery' points to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A globetrotter is someone who travels widely around the world, an experienced voyager.

clue.text: This way cover is continuous

parts.note: so means in this way or thus
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A claim that covering in this manner leaves no gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid can mean unbroken or without interruption, as in a solid line or eight solid hours.

clue.text: Unresting revolutionary?

indicators.note: revolutionary hints at turning things round, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel who never takes a break.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay at once: an insurgent is a revolutionary, and one who cannot rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a rebel rising against authority, so a revolutionary fighter who never stops.

clue.text: Flight crew forgets Irish prayer's ending

indicators.note: forgets means leaves out, so the letters for Irish are dropped from the crew

parts.note: airmen are a crew of fliers

explanation.surface: Aircrew who cannot remember the close of an Irish prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is the word said at the close of a prayer, its traditional final word.

clue.text: East European and English fellow flanked by two Scotsmen

indicators.note: flanked by means having one on each side, so the two Scotsmen go either side

parts.note: Mac is a stock form of address for a Scotsman
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: Someone from Eastern Europe and an Englishman stand between a pair of Scots.
explanation.walkthrough: Mac is a stock address for any Scotsman, and Ian a typically Scottish name; a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: A Macedonian is a native of North Macedonia, a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Number sported by first lady, right for decisive moment?

parts.note: sported means wore, as clothing
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A figure worn by the President's wife is just right for a big occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' looks like the President's wife, but it is EVE, the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a critical point at which a chance must be taken or lost forever.

clue.text: Left among displaced Estonians coming from nowhere?

indicators.note: among means placed in the middle of, so one letter goes inside
displaced means moved out of place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Left with refugees from Estonia who have no homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaced' turns ESTONIANS into NATIONESS, and 'among' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without a country belongs to no nation, so in a playful sense comes from no place.

clue.text: Lower, shorter and lighter

indicators.note: shorter means cut down, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to lower (rhyming with power) is to frown or scowl

explanation.surface: Something is lowered, shortened and made less heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as 'make lower'; it is the verb rhyming with 'power', to scowl. 'Lighter' is not 'less heavy' but a barge.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat, like a lighter that ferries cargo to and from ships.

clue.text: Flaring signal thundered, protecting time and time again

parts.note: a bell is a signal, as a school bell

indicators.note: protecting means guarding round about, so the letters sit inside

parts.note: boomed means made a thunderous noise
T again, a second abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A flare is fired as a signal while thunder rumbles over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts T and T inside BOOMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Bell-bottomed trousers flare out widely below the knee, so the word describes flared legs.

clue.text: One's appearance may confuse person finishing binge after gallons

indicators.note: after means placed behind, so the gallons come first

parts.note: an ender is one who finishes something
a bender is a drinking binge

explanation.surface: A drinker ends a spree after downing gallons and looks confused.
explanation.definitionFit: A gender bender dresses or looks like the opposite sex, so their looks can mislead an observer.

clue.text: Land of extravagant comfort? Go Brum for a change!

parts.note: luxe means luxury, lavish comfort

indicators.note: for a change says the letters are altered, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A travel slogan: swap luxury for a trip to Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: Brum is a nickname for Birmingham, a big English city. 'for a change' turns GO BRUM into MBOURG.
explanation.definitionFit: Luxembourg is a small country in western Europe, a grand duchy.

clue.text: To criticise mentally is fine; to exterminate almost ..?

parts.note: fine means thin, as a fine thread

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: to kill off is to exterminate

explanation.surface: A muddled remark that thinking ill is fine but wiping out is nearly the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last F from KILL OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in low regard privately is to judge them harshly in one's mind.

clue.text: This woman occupies employment time in theatre's confines

definitions.text: This woman occupies employment time in theatre's confines

indicators.note: occupies means fills the space within, so the woman goes inside

parts.note: use means employment, as in putting to use
her refers to this woman

indicators.note: confines are the edges, so take the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A woman works within the walls of a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupies' puts HER in USE; 'confines' gives the first and last letters of theatre, TE. The whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An usherette is a woman who shows people to their seats in a cinema or theatre.

clue.text: Shore bird done in by run to nest

indicators.note: done in means destroyed, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A coastal bird is killed by a sprint back to its nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnstone is a wading bird of shorelines that flips stones for food.

clue.text: Impulsive move to take the edges off appetite after light starter

indicators.note: after means the other part follows, so it comes second
starter means first course, so the first letter is taken
take the edges off means remove the first and last letters

parts.note: hunger is appetite

explanation.surface: A sudden move to curb one's appetite after a light first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take the edges off' strips HUNGER to UNGE; 'starter' gives L from light.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden thrust forward, a rash movement.

clue.text: Bit of neorealism adopted by formerly old-fashioned surrealist artist

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: erst is an archaic word meaning formerly

indicators.note: bit of means just a piece, here the first letter

explanation.surface: Some neorealism is taken up by a once-trendy surrealist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' puts N inside ERST.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German painter, a leading figure of Dada and surrealism.

clue.text: Reason to handle bitter deprivation?

parts.note: a ration is an allowance that deprives, as in wartime rationing
bitter is a type of ale, a British beer

explanation.surface: A justification for coping with a shortage of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British pale ale. Read 'bitter deprivation?' as rationed beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or justification for something.

clue.text: They may rot our teeth anyhow: do we bite less?

indicators.note: anyhow means in a haphazard way, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sweets will damage our teeth whatever we do, even if we chew less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges DO WE BITE LESS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard sugary candies sucked slowly are notorious for causing tooth decay.

clue.text: It's essential to take a selfish stand

indicators.note: It's essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice that one must take up a self-centred position.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds an artist's canvas.

clue.text: Man is one I almost killed

indicators.note: almost means nearly complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: slew is the past tense of slay, to kill

explanation.surface: A confession of nearly killing a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so Man is an example of one.

clue.text: There's something calculated about cold lowlife

indicators.note: about means around, so the sum goes round the letter for cold

parts.note: a sum is something worked out by calculation

explanation.surface: A calculating criminal moves around in cold blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C inside SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum are the lowest, most worthless people, the dregs of society.

clue.text: Sullen girl losing heart when embraced by man losing head

indicators.note: embraced by means held within, so one piece goes inside the other
losing head means the first letter goes

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letters go

parts.note: taken as written, the word girl

explanation.surface: A moody girl gets dispirited in the arms of a dejected man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sullen' fits through the sense of an ugly mood, sulky and threatening, rather than unattractive looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can describe a threatening, bad-tempered mood, as in an ugly temper.

clue.text: Dance tracks like this will captivate leggy birds after maybe 45 minutes

indicators.note: after means coming behind, so the rest follows the time piece

parts.note: forty-five minutes is three-quarters of an hour, so three of the four letters of hour

indicators.note: will captivate means hold within, so the birds go inside

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, meaning like this
emus are long-legged flightless birds

explanation.surface: Dance tunes in this style will charm long-legged birds after three quarters of an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: Forty-five minutes is three-quarters of an hour, so three of the four letters of HOUR give HOU.
explanation.definitionFit: House music is a style of electronic dance music born in Chicago clubs.

clue.text: Fine smoke going round one's home

indicators.note: going round means turned back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Fine cigarette smoke drifts round someone's house.
explanation.walkthrough: A fag is British slang for a cigarette, and a gaff is British slang for one's house or flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaff is British slang for a house or flat, where someone lives.

clue.text: Type of lamp that's guided rafter, say, on the waves

parts.note: sea is what the waves are on
led means guided
a rafter is an example of a beam

explanation.surface: A lamp guiding a roof timber across the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as a beam led over the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealed-beam lamp has its reflector and lens fused as one unit, as in old car headlights.
